Case study: Mishra et al. (2020)

Source: vignettes/mishra-case-study.Rmd
mishra-case-study.Rmd

Mishra et al. (2020) derived the renewal equation from an age-dependent branching process and combined it with a negative binomial observation model to estimate the time-varying reproduction number RtR_t from reported cases. This vignette fits their model to test-confirmed COVID-19 cases from South Korea in early 2020, following the ComposableTuringIDModels.jl tutorial of the same analysis.

library(composableIDModelR)

Data

The package includes daily confirmed cases in South Korea. We fit the first wave, from 13 February to 19 March 2020.

south_korea <- read.csv(
  system.file("extdata", "south_korea_data.csv", package = "composableIDModelR")
)
south_korea$date <- as.Date(south_korea$date)
first_wave <- south_korea[45:80, ]

plot(first_wave$date, first_wave$cases_new, type = "b",
     xlab = "Date", ylab = "Confirmed cases")

Model

The model is

Zt=ρ1Zt−1+ρ2Zt−2+ϵt,ϵt∼Normal(0,σ),Rt=exp⁡(Zt),It=Rt∑s≥1gsIt−s,yt∼NegBinomial(It,ϕ), \begin{aligned} Z_t &= \rho_1 Z_{t-1} + \rho_2 Z_{t-2} + \epsilon_t, & \epsilon_t &\sim \mathrm{Normal}(0, \sigma), \\ R_t &= \exp(Z_t), \\ I_t &= R_t \sum_{s \ge 1} g_s I_{t-s}, \\ y_t &\sim \mathrm{NegBinomial}(I_t, \phi), \end{aligned}

where gsg_s is the discretised generation interval.

The latent log reproduction number follows an AR(2) process. A first damping coefficient concentrated near one encodes strong autocorrelation, and the innovation standard deviation σ\sigma is estimated with a half-normal prior.

latent <- AR(
  damp = list(
    truncated(Normal(0.8, 0.05), 0, 1),
    truncated(Normal(0.1, 0.05), 0, 1)
  ),
  init = list(Normal(0, 0.2), Normal(0, 0.2)),
  epsilon_t = HierarchicalNormal(std = HalfNormal(0.1))
)

The latent process belongs to the renewal model. Following Mishra et al. (2020), a gamma distribution with shape 6.5 and scale 0.62 approximates the generation interval, and is discretised with double interval censoring.

renewal <- Renewal(
  generation_time = Gamma(shape = 6.5, scale = 0.62),
  rt = latent,
  initialisation = Normal(log(1), 0.1)
)

Reported cases are negative binomial. The prior is on the cluster factor 1/ϕ\sqrt{1/\phi}, which is approximately the coefficient of variation of the observation noise.

model <- IDModel(
  renewal,
  NegativeBinomialError(cluster_factor = HalfNormal(0.1))
)
model
#> <composableIDModelR model component>
#> IDModel(
#>     Renewal(;
#>         generation_time = Gamma(6.5, 0.62),
#>         rt = AR(;
#>             damp = [
#>                 truncated(Normal(0.8, 0.05), 0.0, 1.0),
#>                 truncated(Normal(0.1, 0.05), 0.0, 1.0)
#>             ],
#>             init = [Normal(0.0, 0.2), Normal(0.0, 0.2)],
#>             ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(; std = HalfNormal(0.1))
#>         ),
#>         initialisation = Normal(0.0, 0.1)
#>     ),
#>     NegativeBinomialError(; cluster_factor = HalfNormal(0.1))
#> )

Fit

We run four chains with a raised target acceptance rate, which keeps the sampler stable on the hierarchical innovation scale. The chains are kept short so the vignette builds quickly.

fitted <- fit(
  model,
  first_wave$cases_new,
  dates = first_wave$date,
  method = nuts(draws = 500, warmup = 500, chains = 4,
                target_acceptance = 0.95),
  seed = 1234
)
#> Starting Julia ...
fitted
#> <composableIDModelR fit>
#> Model:
#>   IDModel(
#>       Renewal(;
#>           generation_time = Gamma(6.5, 0.62),
#>           rt = AR(;
#>               damp = [
#>                   truncated(Normal(0.8, 0.05), 0.0, 1.0),
#>                   truncated(Normal(0.1, 0.05), 0.0, 1.0)
#>               ],
#>               init = [Normal(0.0, 0.2), Normal(0.0, 0.2)],
#>               ϵ_t = HierarchicalNormal(; std = HalfNormal(0.1))
#>           ),
#>           initialisation = Normal(0.0, 0.1)
#>       ),
#>       NegativeBinomialError(; cluster_factor = HalfNormal(0.1))
#>   )
#> 
#> Data: 36 time points
#> Sampling: 4 chains of 500 draws after 500 warmup
#> 
#> Convergence:
#>   Max Rhat: 1.03 
#>   Min bulk ESS: 100 
#>   Divergent transitions: 7 
#> 
#> Use summary() for parameter estimates and plot() to visualise.

The printout reports some divergent transitions, so for a real analysis the chains should be run for longer and the divergences investigated, for example with the sampler diagnostics in fitted$sampler.

Parameters are named after the component that samples them: damp_AR are the damping coefficients ρ\rho, std is σ\sigma, cluster_factor is the observation cluster factor, and init_incidence is the log initial incidence. The standardised innovations ϵ_t are omitted here.

summary(fitted) |>
  subset(!startsWith(variable, "ϵ_t"))
#> # A tibble: 7 × 10
#>   variable     mean   median     sd    mad      q5   q95  rhat ess_bulk ess_tail
#>   <chr>       <dbl>    <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>

The draws are a posterior::draws_df, so all of the posterior tooling applies.

posterior::subset_draws(
  posterior::as_draws_df(fitted),
  variable = c("damp_AR", "std", "cluster_factor")
) |>
  posterior::summarise_draws("mean", "sd", "rhat", "ess_bulk")
#> # A tibble: 4 × 5
#>   variable         mean     sd  rhat ess_bulk
#>   <chr>           <dbl>  <dbl> <dbl>    <dbl>
#> 1 damp_AR[1]     0.817  0.0417  1.01     449.
#> 2 damp_AR[2]     0.0813 0.0405  1.01     310.
#> 3 std            0.419  0.0472  1.01     290.
#> 4 cluster_factor 0.0958 0.0657  1.02     100.

Results

The reproduction number rises well above one early in the wave, falls through one as cases peak, and stays below one as cases decline.

plot(fitted, type = "Rt")

The posterior predictive distribution tracks the observed cases.

plot(fitted, type = "cases")

Swapping the observation model

Reported cases lag infections by the incubation period. Adding a log-normal delay (mean of about 5 days) changes only the observation model:

delayed_model <- IDModel(
  renewal,
  LatentDelay(
    NegativeBinomialError(cluster_factor = HalfNormal(0.1)),
    delay = LogNormal(1.6, 0.42)
  )
)

delayed <- fit(
  delayed_model,
  first_wave$cases_new,
  dates = first_wave$date,
  method = nuts(draws = 500, warmup = 500, chains = 4,
                target_acceptance = 0.95),
  seed = 1234
)
plot(delayed, type = "Rt")

Accounting for the delay moves the decline in RtR_t earlier, because infections precede the cases they cause.

References

Mishra, S., Berah, T., Mellan, T. A., et al. (2020). On the derivation of the renewal equation from an age-dependent branching process: an epidemic modelling perspective. arXiv:2006.16487.
